items.q: Ali shares 12 sweets equally among 3 friends. How many sweets does each friend get?
items.hint: Deal the sweets one at a time to each friend.
steps: Deal one sweet at a time to each of the 3 friends.
Count the sweets one friend has.

slips.say: 3 is the number of friends. How many sweets does each friend get?

tpl.q: Ali shares {t} sweets equally among {a} friends. How many sweets does each friend get?
tpl.hint: Deal the sweets one at a time to each friend.
steps: Deal one sweet at a time to each of the {a} friends.
Count the sweets one friend has.

items.q: Mei puts 12 cookies into bags. She puts 3 cookies in each bag. How many bags does Mei need?
items.hint: Make groups of 3 until the cookies are gone.
steps: Make a group of 3 cookies, again and again.

slips.say: 3 is the number of cookies in each bag. How many bags?

tpl.q: Mei puts {t} cookies into bags. She puts {b} cookies in each bag. How many bags does Mei need?
tpl.hint: Make groups of {b} until the cookies are gone.
steps: Make a group of {b} cookies, again and again.

items.q: Ravi puts 15 stickers into bags of 5. Is this share or group?
items.hint: The story says how many are in each bag.
steps: The story tells us 5 stickers are in each bag.
So Ravi puts the stickers into groups of 5.

slips.say: Does the story tell us how many bags, or how many stickers are in each bag?

items.q: Siti gives 16 beads equally to 4 friends. Is this share or group?
items.hint: The story says how many friends.
steps: The story tells us there are 4 friends.
Siti deals the beads out equally.

slips.say: Does the story tell us how many friends, or how many beads are in each group?

items.q: Check it. 4 friends each get 3 stickers. How many stickers were shared in all?
steps: 4 friends with 3 stickers each is 4 groups of 3.

slips.say: 7 is 4 + 3. Make 4 groups with 3 in each group.

tpl.q: Check it. {a} friends each get {b} stickers. How many stickers were shared in all?
tpl.hint: {a} groups of {b}. Add {b} again and again.
steps: {a} friends with {b} stickers each is {a} groups of {b}.

items.q: Ali has 14 counters. He puts them into groups of 4. How many groups can he make?
items.hint: Make groups of 4 until there are not enough for another group.
steps: 2 counters are left. That is not enough for another group.

slips.say: There are not enough counters for a fourth group of 4.

tpl.q: Ali has {t} counters. He puts them into groups of {b}. How many groups can he make?
tpl.hint: Make groups of {b} until there are not enough for another group.
steps: {c} counters are left. That is not enough for another group.

items.q: Mei has 17 stickers. She puts 5 stickers in each bag. How many stickers are left over?
items.hint: Fill bags of 5. Count what is left.

slips.say: 3 is the number of bags. How many stickers are left over?

tpl.q: Mei has {t} stickers. She puts {b} stickers in each bag. How many stickers are left over?
tpl.hint: Fill bags of {b}. Count what is left.

items.q: Ben shares 20 biscuits equally with his 3 cousins. How many biscuits does each person get?
items.hint: Count Ben too. How many people share the biscuits?
steps: Ben and his 3 cousins share: 4 people.

slips.say: Count Ben too: 4 people share, not 3.

tpl.q: Ben shares {t} biscuits equally with his {c} cousins. How many biscuits does each person get?

items.q: Ravi has 17 stickers. He puts 5 stickers in each bag. How many more stickers does he need to fill one more bag?
items.hint: Find how many are left over. Then see how many more make a full bag.

slips.say: 2 is how many are left over. How many more make 5?

tpl.q: Ravi has {t} stickers. He puts {b} stickers in each bag. How many more stickers does he need to fill one more bag?
tpl.hint: Find how many are left over. Then see how many more make a full bag.

items.q: Type every number of friends from 1 to 12 who can share 12 sweets equally with none left over. Put a comma between the numbers.
items.hint: Try 1, 2, 3 and so on. Does each number leave none left over?
steps: 1 friend gets 12. 2 friends get 6. 3 friends get 4.
4 friends get 3. 6 friends get 2. 12 friends get 1.

tpl.q: Type every number of friends from 1 to {t} who can share {t} sweets equally with none left over. Put a comma between the numbers.
tpl.hint: Try 1, 2, 3 and so on. Does each number leave none left over?
steps: Try each number of friends from 1 up.
Keep the numbers with none left over.

items.q: Jenny shares 20 pencils equally among 4 pots. Then she puts 3 more pencils in each pot. How many pencils are in each pot now?
items.hint: Share first. Then add to each pot.
steps: 20 pencils among 4 pots is 5 in each pot.

slips.say: 5 is how many at first. Add the 3 more pencils.

tpl.q: Jenny shares {t} pencils equally among {a} pots. Then she puts {m} more pencils in each pot. How many pencils are in each pot now?
tpl.hint: Share first. Then add to each pot.
steps: {t} pencils among {a} pots is {b} in each pot.

items.q: Wei has 20 stickers. He keeps 2. He shares the rest equally among 3 friends. How many stickers does each friend get?
items.hint: Take away the stickers Wei keeps. Then share the rest.

slips.say: Take away the 2 stickers Wei keeps before you share.

items.q: Make a sharing puzzle for a grown-up. Use 12 counters. Ask: how many plates, and how many on each plate? Many answers are right.
items.hint: Pick the number of plates first. Then deal the counters.
steps: Deal the 12 counters one at a time.
Check: plates times counters on each plate makes 12.
